beats.speaker: tilly
beats.voiceover: Jupiter is ridiculous. It's eleven Earths wide.

beats.speaker: tilly
beats.voiceover: Split it open and there's no ground. Just hydrogen squeezed into liquid, then liquid that acts like metal, around a fuzzy core.

beats.speaker: tilly
beats.voiceover: It's also heavy. More than twice as heavy as every other planet put together.

views.subtitle: the mass of all other planets combined

beats.speaker: tilly
beats.voiceover: And it spins fast. One day here? Under ten hours.

beats.speaker: tilly
beats.voiceover: That red spot is a storm bigger than Earth. It's been going for over a hundred years.

beats.speaker: tilly
beats.voiceover: It barely leans, just three degrees. So, hardly any seasons.

beats.speaker: tilly
beats.voiceover: Juno pulled into orbit in 2016. Okay, review time. Size: five out of five. Landing spots: zero.

claims.claim: Jupiter is 11 times wider than Earth (on screen: "11 Earths wide"; Earth drawn at 0.09 of Jupiter's diameter).
claims.source: NASA Science, Jupiter Facts: "With a radius of 43,440.7 miles (69,911 kilometers), Jupiter is 11 times wider than Earth." https://science.nasa.gov/jupiter/jupiter-facts/ ; NASA NSSDC Jupiter Fact Sheet, equatorial radius ratio Jupiter/Earth 11.209 (1 ÷ 11.209 = 0.089) https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/jupiterfact.html

claims.claim: Jupiter has no solid ground: as a gas giant it has no true surface (on screen: "No solid surface").
claims.source: NASA Science, Jupiter Facts: "As a gas giant, Jupiter doesn't have a true surface." https://science.nasa.gov/jupiter/jupiter-facts/

claims.claim: Deep inside, pressure squeezes Jupiter's hydrogen gas into a liquid, and deeper still the liquid conducts electricity like a metal (labels: "Hydrogen gas", "Liquid hydrogen", "Metallic hydrogen").
claims.source: NASA Science, Jupiter Facts: "Deep in the atmosphere, pressure and temperature increase, compressing the hydrogen gas into a liquid" and "making the liquid electrically conducting like metal". https://science.nasa.gov/jupiter/jupiter-facts/
claims.note: The layers in the cutaway are a diagram; their thicknesses are not to scale and no sizes are stated.

claims.claim: Jupiter's core is described by researchers as dilute, or "fuzzy" (label: "Fuzzy core").
claims.source: NASA Science, Jupiter Facts: "leading researchers to describe the core as dilute, or 'fuzzy.'" https://science.nasa.gov/jupiter/jupiter-facts/

claims.claim: Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined (on screen: "Over 2×", "the mass of all other planets combined").
claims.source: NASA Science, Jupiter overview: "more than twice as massive as the other planets combined." https://science.nasa.gov/jupiter/

claims.claim: One day on Jupiter takes 9.9 hours, which is under ten hours (on screen: "1 day = 9.9 hours").
claims.source: NASA Science, Jupiter Facts: "One day on Jupiter takes 9.9 hours" https://science.nasa.gov/jupiter/jupiter-facts/ ; NASA NSSDC Jupiter Fact Sheet, length of day 9.9259 hours https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/jupiterfact.html

claims.claim: The Great Red Spot is a storm bigger than Earth (on screen: "Great Red Spot", "A storm bigger than Earth").
claims.source: NASA Science, Jupiter Facts: "Jupiter's iconic Great Red Spot is a giant storm bigger than Earth that has raged for hundreds of years." https://science.nasa.gov/jupiter/jupiter-facts/

claims.claim: The Great Red Spot has been going for over a hundred years.
claims.source: NASA Science, Jupiter Facts: "has raged for hundreds of years" and "has been observed on the giant planet for more than 300 years." https://science.nasa.gov/jupiter/jupiter-facts/
claims.note: Conservative on purpose: NASA says hundreds of years, but whether the spot seen in the 1600s is the same storm is debated, so the script only says "over a hundred years".

claims.claim: Jupiter's equator is tilted just 3 degrees to its orbit, so its seasons are mild (on screen: 3 degrees, "spin axis", "orbit").
claims.source: NASA Science, Jupiter Facts: "Its equator is tilted with respect to its orbital path around the Sun by just 3 degrees. This means Jupiter spins nearly upright and does not have seasons as extreme as other planets do." https://science.nasa.gov/jupiter/jupiter-facts/ ; NASA NSSDC Jupiter Fact Sheet, obliquity to orbit 3.13 degrees https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/jupiterfact.html
claims.note: NASA says the seasons are not as extreme as on other planets; the script says "hardly any seasons", not "none".

claims.claim: NASA's Juno spacecraft entered orbit around Jupiter in 2016 (on screen: "Juno · arrived 2016").
claims.source: NASA Science, Jupiter Exploration: "the Juno spacecraft entered orbit around Jupiter on July 4, 2016." https://science.nasa.gov/jupiter/exploration/

claims.claim: There is nowhere to land on Jupiter ("Landing spots: zero").
claims.source: NASA Science, Jupiter Facts: "As a gas giant, Jupiter doesn't have a true surface." https://science.nasa.gov/jupiter/jupiter-facts/
claims.note: The "five out of five" rating is Tilly's opinion, not a fact.

publish.title: Strange facts about Jupiter
publish.description: Eleven Earths wide, no ground to stand on, a day under ten hours and a storm bigger than our whole planet. Tilly reviews Jupiter.
